geography.notes: California Energy Commission solicitation; project must qualify under the solicitation and eligible federal geothermal funding opportunity.

hardRequirements: Applicant must apply for and receive an award under an eligible federal geothermal funding opportunity.
CEC funds are cost-share only and must meet GFO-25-902 solicitation requirements.
blockers: Do not match to ground_source_geothermal_heat_pump; the source supports geothermal energy funding cost-share, not building HVAC heat-pump installations.
Not a residential or commercial building retrofit rebate.
repairs.evidenceText: CEC lists GFO-25-902 as active grant funding that provides cost-share funding to applicants receiving eligible federal geothermal awards.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Input target list from uploaded file . Removed the ground-source heat-pump match because the official solicitation is for federal geothermal award cost share, not building HVAC retrofits.

geography.notes: Massachusetts municipalities designated as Green Communities; grants apply to municipal/public clean energy and efficiency projects.

hardRequirements: Applicant must be a designated Massachusetts Green Community or otherwise eligible under the current DOER grant round.
Projects must be municipal clean energy, energy efficiency, decarbonization, or technical-assistance projects approved by DOER.
blockers: Not open to private residential or commercial customers.
Do not match as a generic building-controls rebate outside municipal Green Communities grant rounds.
repairs.evidenceText: Massachusetts DOER describes Green Communities grants as support for municipal clean energy and efficiency projects; 2026 awards include conservation measures and Building Management System replacement.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The energy-management match is supported only in the municipal Green Communities context. Source confidence is medium because some current Mass.gov program pages were partially inaccessible, but official snippets and award documents corroborate current activity.

geography.notes: Limited to Green Mountain Power customer premises in Vermont.

hardRequirements: Customer must have a compatible home battery system and enroll it for GMP peak-event discharge.
Customer must maintain internet connectivity and allow GMP dispatch under the BYOD agreement.
Battery must be used for home backup power and program purposes at the enrolled premises.
blockers: Not a stand-alone solar PV incentive.
Do not match to generic batteries outside GMP territory or to systems that cannot be controlled for GMP peak events.
repairs.evidenceText: GMP BYOD offers battery rebates for customers who share stored energy during peak events; eligible home battery systems and incentive rates are listed.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The battery-storage match is source-backed. Added demand-response limitation because the rebate is tied to GMP control of enrolled behind-the-meter batteries.

geography.notes: SDG&E service territory; lodging businesses with eligible NAICS codes.

hardRequirements: Customer must have an active SDG&E electric or gas account and pay the Public Purpose Program surcharge.
Facility must be in eligible lodging NAICS categories and provide at least twelve consecutive months of energy data.
Projects may not double-count incentives with other energy-efficiency programs and must satisfy NMEC and program screening requirements.
blockers: Remove automated_demand_response_controls match; GRID-Lodging is a meter-based energy-efficiency incentive, not a demand response controls rebate.
Not for non-lodging facilities or customers outside SDG&E territory.
repairs.evidenceText: SDG&E lists GRID-Lodging for hotels and motels; the program rewards SDG&E lodging customers for qualifying projects that save energy.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Corrected false-positive demand-response match. The official SDG&E listing and implementer page support custom/metered energy efficiency only.

geography.notes: Applies in Guam to qualifying real property improvements with photovoltaic solar panels or photovoltaic roof tiles installed on buildings.

hardRequirements: Photovoltaic solar panels or photovoltaic roof tiles must be installed on a building.
The incentive is an exclusion of added photovoltaic value from real-property improvements for tax assessment purposes.
blockers: Not a cash rebate, grant, or utility incentive.
Do not match to battery storage, solar water heating, or non-photovoltaic roofing measures.
repairs.evidenceText: Guam real property tax code excludes value added by photovoltaic solar panels and photovoltaic roof tiles installed on buildings from taxable improvements.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Current official Guam tax pages were not located in a readily accessible form; DSIRE and public code text support the photovoltaic-only match with medium source confidence.

geography.notes: Harris County, Texas; commercial green building tax abatement.

hardRequirements: Project must be new commercial construction registered with USGBC or an equivalent GBCI-administered rating system.
Applicant must file Harris County Green Building Tax Abatement application and required documentation before eligible construction milestones.
Final abatement depends on achieved certification level and County approval.
blockers: Not a rebate for individual equipment measures or general retrofits.
Not for residential buildings; LEED or equivalent green-building certification is the supported matching basis.
repairs.evidenceText: Harris County’s application requires LEED or equivalent GBCI rating-system registration for new commercial construction seeking green-building tax abatement.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The LEED/certification match is source-backed but is not a physical retrofit. Kept only certification-oriented categories and blocked discrete equipment matching.

geography.notes: Statewide Hawaii NEVI deployment focused on designated Alternative Fuel Corridors and public fast-charging sites.

hardRequirements: NEVI-funded chargers must satisfy federal and state corridor, availability, power, reliability, and payment-access requirements.
Initial deployments prioritize public DC fast charging along designated Alternative Fuel Corridors or state-selected sites.
blockers: Not a residential, workplace, or general Level 2 charger rebate.
No current public grant application URL was verified; matching should not imply an open customer rebate.
repairs.evidenceText: HDOT’s Hawaii NEVI page and plan describe formula funding for EV charging infrastructure and public DC fast-charging deployment under NEVI requirements.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The EV-charger match is source-backed, but this is a state NEVI implementation program rather than an open building retrofit rebate.

geography.notes: Solarize Summit serves local residents and businesses; some local rebates are limited to listed municipalities and unincorporated Summit County.

hardRequirements: Participant must use the Solarize Summit program process and installer for Solarize discounts.
For the 2026 campaign, contract deadlines and local rebate funding limits apply.
Local government discounts are limited by residence or business location and are first-come, first-served.
blockers: Not a statewide Colorado solar rebate.
Battery storage is eligible only as part of the Solarize Summit offering; do not generalize to unrelated storage incentives.
repairs.evidenceText: Solarize Summit’s 2026 page offers limited-time discounts on solar panel installation and battery storage for local residents and certain businesses.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The rooftop solar match is supported. Added battery storage because the current official page includes battery storage; geography and campaign-deadline limits are material.

geography.notes: HG&E gas or electric service customers; properties generally four units or fewer.

hardRequirements: Applicant must own an eligible property served by HG&E gas or electric service and have accounts in good standing.
Many efficiency projects require a free home energy audit before loan approval.
Quotes, deed verification, applicable permits, program fees, and lien/loan documents may be required.
blockers: Remove standalone energy_audit as the financed retrofit; the audit is generally a prerequisite for funded measures.
Renters are not eligible applicants, and most new construction or gut rehabilitation is excluded except stated measure exceptions.
repairs.evidenceText: HG&E REAP offers zero-interest financing for residential efficiency, electrification, weatherization, solar, battery, EV charging, and related measures.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The source supports many eligible measures, but the original energy-audit match was too broad because audits are prerequisites or services rather than the financed retrofit itself.

geography.notes: Iowa businesses and industries, with priority for manufacturers and projects with quantifiable efficiency gains.

hardRequirements: Project must be in Iowa and produce quantifiable energy-efficiency or related savings.
Loan terms and eligibility depend on IADG Energy Bank underwriting and program availability.
Borrowers generally must be businesses or industries, with priority for manufacturers.
blockers: Do not match as a generic energy management system rebate for buildings.
Not residential; this is revolving-loan financing, not a rebate or grant for any listed measure.
repairs.evidenceText: IADG describes the Energy Bank as revolving loan support for Iowa businesses and industries undertaking qualifying energy-efficiency equipment and related projects.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Current official details are limited but support financing for industrial/business efficiency projects. The original energy-management match was narrowed to financing-eligible industrial measures.

geography.notes: Idaho Falls Power commercial and industrial electric customers.

hardRequirements: Customer must receive electricity from Idaho Falls Power.
Energy audit or pre-inspection is required before purchase, installation, or custom project approval.
Loan limits, minimum project cost, administrative fee, and program-specific technical requirements apply.
blockers: Remove standalone energy_audit match; audit is a required step, not the funded measure.
Not for residential customers and not for projects installed before required IFP review.
repairs.evidenceText: Idaho Falls Power offers commercial zero-interest loans or rebates for HVAC, lighting, insulation, controls, and custom efficiency projects after required audits.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The audit term caused a false-positive match. Repaired categories to actual commercial and industrial funded measures.

geography.notes: IID service area; commercial customers with eligible custom energy-efficiency projects.

hardRequirements: Customer must be in IID service territory and apply for preliminary energy analysis before implementation.
Installed equipment must exceed Title 24 or current industry-standard baselines as applicable.
Incentives are based on annual kWh savings and subject to available program funding.
blockers: Not a residential appliance rebate.
Do not match to refrigeration unless the project is a qualifying commercial custom efficiency measure in IID territory.
repairs.evidenceText: IID’s Custom Energy Solutions Program pays commercial incentives for lighting, refrigeration, HVAC, food service, agricultural, process, and control equipment savings.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The refrigeration match is supported, but only as part of IID’s commercial custom energy-efficiency incentive.

geography.notes: Illinois NEVI corridor fast-charging deployment; applications and awards are administered by IDOT.

hardRequirements: Projects must comply with Illinois NEVI solicitation requirements, federal NEVI charging standards, uptime, public access, and corridor siting requirements.
Initial phases focus on DC fast charging stations along Alternative Fuel Corridors.
blockers: No current open IDOT application round was verified as of 2026-07-02; prior application rounds are closed.
Not a residential or workplace Level 2 charging rebate.
repairs.evidenceText: IDOT’s NEVI page describes DC fast-charging corridor deployment and prior application rounds; Round 3’s listed deadline has passed.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The EV charger category is correct for NEVI DC fast charging, but availability was corrected to temporarily closed for new applicants.

geography.notes: Indiana NEVI deployment along state Alternative Fuel Corridors and major highways; awards handled through INDOT.

hardRequirements: Projects must comply with Indiana NEVI contracting, federal NEVI standards, public access, uptime, and corridor-siting requirements.
Award recipients must provide required non-federal cost share and meet INDOT contract obligations.
blockers: No current open application round was verified; INDOT describes resuming contracting for prior contingent awards and future phases to be announced.
Not a general customer EV charger rebate.
repairs.evidenceText: Indiana’s Charging the Crossroads site describes NEVI-funded EV charging along interstates and highways, with prior awards moving through contracting.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The EV-charger match is source-backed but should not appear as currently open for new general applications.

geography.notes: Indiana Michigan Power residential customers in Indiana.

hardRequirements: Customer must be a residential I&M customer with an EV and Level 2 charger.
Customer may not be enrolled in Net Metering Service Rider or Excess Distributed Generation Rider.
Charging must occur during the designated 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. window or through managed Charge Sync Plus events to earn credits.
blockers: Remove ev_charger_installation match; current program is a managed/off-peak charging bill-credit program, not a charger purchase or installation rebate.
Only supported EVs or chargers may enroll; customers may be in only one I&M EV program at a time.
repairs.evidenceText: I&M’s current Indiana page offers Charge Sync Rewards bill credits for residential customers with EVs and Level 2 chargers who charge at approved times.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The current official page no longer supports a physical charger-installation rebate match; retained only managed charging as the eligible category.

geography.notes: SVP business page points qualifying facilities to San Jose State University Industrial Assessment Center services.

hardRequirements: Facility must meet SJSU Industrial Assessment Center eligibility, such as manufacturing or wastewater facility type and energy-bill thresholds, unless otherwise approved.
Assessment produces recommendations; implementation incentives or rebates are separate programs.
blockers: Remove low_flow_fixture_retrofit match; the word fixture does not support a plumbing or water-efficiency retrofit category.
This is no-cost technical assistance, not a direct equipment rebate.
repairs.evidenceText: SVP lists no-cost industrial assessments by SJSU IAC; the assessment report recommends energy-saving measures, costs, incentives, and payback.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The original fixture-based low-flow match was unsupported. Repaired to technical assessment/audit categories only.

geography.notes: JEA non-residential electric service customers and commercial fleet sites in the JEA service area.

hardRequirements: Make-ready applicants must have an active JEA non-residential electric service account and the facility must be within JEA electric service territory.
Make-ready infrastructure must support EVSE for fleet electrification and generally requires new or upgraded electric service.
Eligible make-ready costs are limited to specified utility-side or up-to-meter customer responsibilities and capped by program rules.
blockers: Not a residential EV charging program.

Make-ready incentives do not cover behind-the-meter electrical upgrades, chargers, networking equipment, bollards, maintenance, or software under the make-ready category; separate ERP charger rebates may apply.
repairs.evidenceText: JEA’s fleet program offers fleet conversion support plus a make-ready incentive up to $15,000 or 60% of eligible project cost.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The original make-ready match is supported. Added boundaries between fleet planning, make-ready infrastructure, and separate ERP charger/electrification rebates.

geography.notes: KIUC members on Kauaʻi; loan partner is Gather Federal Credit Union.

hardRequirements: Member must replace an existing electric water heater or non-functioning solar water heater with a whole solar water-heater system including panels and tank.
Application must be initiated through a KIUC participating solar contractor.
Loan is zero-interest through Gather Federal Credit Union, subject to credit approval and program requirements.
blockers: Not solar PV, heat pump water heater, or water-heater timer; those are separate KIUC offerings.
Do not combine the rebate and loan for the same installation.
repairs.evidenceText: KIUC members replacing existing electric or failed solar water heaters may apply for a zero-interest loan for whole-system solar water heater installations.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The solar water heating match is source-backed. Loan-specific repair separates financing from the companion rebate and from other water-heater incentives.

geography.notes: KIUC members on Kauaʻi using participating solar contractors.

hardRequirements: Member must replace an existing electric water heater or non-functioning solar water heater with a whole solar water-heater system including panels and tank.
Rebate application is handled through a KIUC participating solar contractor.
Program funds and contractor participation requirements apply.
blockers: Not solar PV, heat pump water heater, or water-heater timer; those are separate KIUC offerings.
Do not combine the rebate and zero-interest loan for the same solar water heater installation.
repairs.evidenceText: KIUC’s current water heating page offers a $1,500 rebate for whole-system solar water heater installations replacing eligible existing water heaters.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The solar water heating match is correct. The repair distinguishes the rebate from the companion loan and from separate heat-pump and timer rebates.

utilityTerritories: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power
geography.notes: Projects must be within LADWP service territory; Owens Valley pricing applies only where allowed by program rules.

hardRequirements: Applicant must submit a complete hard-copy FiT application package with required fees, deposits, and forms.
Project must be in LADWP service territory and applicant must demonstrate site control and qualified project-development experience.
Output is sold directly to LADWP under a Standard Offer Power Purchase Agreement for up to 20 years.
blockers: Do not match as a behind-the-meter rooftop solar rebate, net-metering program, or customer bill-saving incentive.
FiT+ solar-plus-storage is a related but separate pilot program with separate application and eligibility rules.
repairs.administrator: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power
repairs.evidenceText: LADWP FiT buys output from local eligible renewable energy projects, with available capacity updated June 2026 and hard-copy applications required.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Solar PV is supported only as a feed-in-tariff renewable generation project. Replaced generic rooftop_solar_pv with front-of-meter and tariff-specific categories.
